# Table

Section header carries the title and the toolbar. Under the header come the table, then the footer (range, page size, Pagination), and the empty state box in place of both when there are no rows. Pass the table as `children` (a `StaticTable`, `DynamicTable` or `TreeTable`), or name a `kind` and pass its props as `tableProps`. Choose the kind by what people do with the rows: nesting is a Tree table; sort, filter, select, page, expand or row actions is a Dynamic table; otherwise it is a Static table. Every other prop goes to the Section (`title`, `description`, `actions`, `toolbar`, `tabs`).

Also asked as: list of records, data table on a page, sortable list, records with filters, rows and columns, grid, table pattern.

## Usage

A table sits in a Section and spans it. Its first and last cells sit flush with the section edge. The Section header carries the views, then Search and the "Field: value" filters with the record count. The bulk bar is never in the Section header: while rows are selected, a Dynamic table's head row becomes it, so the header rows stay put. Empty and no results replace the whole table so the Section header stays usable; loading and error states happen inside the table, under its header. Paging stays under the rows, inside the same Section.

### Type guidance

Choose by what people do with the rows. Read the questions in order and stop at the first yes.

| Question | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Does any row nest under another? Nesting wins, even when the table is interactive. | Tree table |
| Can people act on the table: sort, filter, select, page, expand rows or use row actions? | Dynamic table |
| Otherwise, people only read it. | Static table |

Search, filters and actions sit in the Section header: `<Table title="Students" views={...} search={...} filters={[...]} count="340 students" kind="dynamic" tableProps={...} />`. Pass the table as `children` instead of `kind` when you build it yourself.

## Motion

Table reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| selection | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Ticking a row turns the head row into the bulk bar: labels cross-fade, same row, same height, nothing slides. Selected rows take the selected fill. The view bar above never moves. |

## Best practices

### Put a plain table in a Section. {#put-a-plain-table-in-a-section}

Do: The table spans the Section under its header: no frame, no card, no padding of its own.
Don't: The table sits inside its own frame with padding. It stops lining up with the Section and the Section header.

### Put nothing between the header and the head row. {#put-nothing-between-the-header-and-the-head-row}

Do: Search, filters and the record count live in the Section header rows. The head row follows directly.
Don't: A second toolbar sits between the Section header and the head row. The table has no toolbar of its own.

### One table per block. {#one-table-per-block}

Never mix a Static, Dynamic or Tree table in one Section either.

Do: One table per Section, with its own header, so people always know which rows its Search and filters act on.
Don't: Two tables share one Section and one header. Search and filters no longer say which table they act on.

### Use a Dynamic table for rows people act on. {#use-a-dynamic-table-for-rows-people-act-on}

Do: A roster people act on as a Dynamic table: sortable heads, checkboxes, a pager, and bulk actions in the head row while rows are selected.
Don't: A roster people act on as a Static table. With no sort, selection or paging, 340 students become one long scroll.

### Use a Tree table for a hierarchy. {#use-a-tree-table-for-a-hierarchy}

Do: Classes nest under their school and students under their class. Each level indents and keeps the columns.
Don't: A hierarchy faked with expandable rows: the classes and students lose their columns and can't be sorted or selected.

## Accessibility

- Name every column with a head cell. Head cells are labels for a column, so they use Heading/xxs rather than a heading level.
- Mark the sorted column with `aria-sort`, and give every icon-only control a name, such as "Actions for Ava Thompson".
- Mark a selected row with `aria-selected="true"`. That attribute belongs to a row of a table with `role="grid"`.
- Selection is never color alone. The row's checkbox is checked, and the head row says "2 selected".
- A region that scrolls takes keyboard focus, so people can scroll it without a pointer. That covers a region with `maxHeight` and one with a sticky column.
- When empty, the empty state replaces the table with no table roles left behind, and keeps the table's accessible name when one was provided.
- Name the table with its `label`, or `label` on the template for the empty state box, when no caption names it.

Same group: `AiChat` · `Frame` · `Modal` · `Page` · `PatternCard` · `PatternSection`

## Parts

1. **Head row.** Names the columns. Its rule is the bold border.
2. **Rows.** The data you pass as `tbody`. Each draws a thin rule, and there is no zebra striping.
3. **Footer** (optional). The `footer` slot under the rows, aligned to the end: the range, the page-size Select and Pagination. It hides while the empty state shows. A Dynamic table draws its own.
4. **Empty state.** The `emptyState` slot, which replaces the whole table (head row, caption and footer included) when `empty` is true; with `empty` and no `emptyState`, the table renders normally.

### States

Row states are layered over each cell's fill, never swapped for it.

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | No fill of its own: the table shows what it sits on. |
| Hovered | The row takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | The row takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed`. |
| Focused | A scroll region takes keyboard focus and draws the `--ds-border-focused` ring. |
| Disabled | A table has no disabled state. Disable the controls in a row. |
| Selected | A row with `aria-selected="true"` takes `--ds-background-selected` across the whole row, with `-hovered` and `-pressed` steps and no stripe on its leading edge. |
| Empty | The empty state replaces the whole table; no head row or footer stays. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name every column with a short head, in sentence case: "Last session". | A blank head, or one in all caps. |
| Give the count in words in the header: "340 students". | A count in the head row or under the table. |
| An empty message that says what will appear and the first action: "No members yet", "Invite a member". | An empty table body with no message. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `kind` | enum | — | The kind of table to draw when no table is passed as `children` |
| `tableProps` | object | — | Props for the table a `kind` draws: its head, rows, label and state |
| `children` | node | — | The table itself, a `StaticTable`, `DynamicTable` or `TreeTable`; wins over `kind` |
| `footer` | node | — | Footer slot under the table (range, page-size Select, Pagination); hidden while the empty state shows |
| `emptyState` | node | — | Empty-state slot: replaces the table and footer when `empty` is true |
| `empty` | bool | `false` | Replace the table with the `emptyState` slot; with `empty` and no `emptyState`, the table renders normally |
| `label` | string | — | The table's accessible name, kept on the empty state box when the table is replaced |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |

## Variants

**`kind`** — `static` · `dynamic` · `tree`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.
